newsitem.title: FINLAND: YRITYSPANKKI SKOP SELLS VIRGIN ISLAND HOTEL.
newsitem.headline: YRITYSPANKKI SKOP SELLS VIRGIN ISLAND HOTEL.

text.p: Finnish bank Yrityspankki SKOP Oy said on Friday it had sealed a deal to sell a hotel and related resort properties in the Virgin Islands to Westin Hotel Company of the U.S. for about $40 million.
"The sale price is about $40 million," Yrityspankki said in a statement.
The hotel came into the hands of Yrityspankki's predecessor SKOPBank in 1995 after it was realised as collaterol for credits granted, the bank said.
State-owned commercial bank Yrityspankki is what remains of SKOPBank, which fell into the state's hands in 1991.
"As a result of the sale, SKOP will be relieved of the significant maintenance costs of the hotel," it said.

The bank said that reserves set aside in SKOP's 1995 financial statements for credit losses and forex risks would be used to cover losses resulting from the sale of the hotel.It did not say how big the loss will be.
